summary_of_change:
Texas Pacific Land's financial results over the latest four quarters highlight tremendous cash conversion alongside clear operational deceleration in completion-sensitive segments. In Q2 2026, consolidated revenue reached $246.1 million (an annualized run-rate of $984.4 million, up 31.2% year-over-year), while gross margin held at an elite 93.3%. Net oil and gas royalty production reached 39.7 kBoe/d (+19.6% year-over-year), driven by the successful integration of 17,306 net royalty acres acquired across the Midland Basin in late 2025. Consolidated quarterly net income stood at $153.9 million with free cash flow of $155.5 million, highlighting the unencumbered cash mechanics of an entity with zero drilling capital commitments.

However, operational deceleration is evident under the surface. Sourced water sales volumes contracted 19.1% sequentially from 820 kbbl/d in Q1 2026 to 663 kbbl/d in Q2 2026 as E&Ps paused completion activity in response to depressed regional gas realizations. Produced water royalty handling grew modestly to 4.9 Mbbl/d, but per-barrel monetization faced mix-shift pressure as volumes shifted from high-margin injection wells to long-haul pipeline easements. Furthermore, net line-of-sight well inventory dropped to 18.4 net wells, confirming that recent volume growth has been fueled by lateral length extension (averaging >11,500 feet) and DUC conversion rather than rig fleet expansion.

Capital allocation has also diverged from its historical playbook. Management completely paused common share repurchases ($0 buybacks over consecutive quarters) to accumulate a minimum liquidity reserve of $700.0 million. Concurrently, capital has been redirected toward $110.2 million in non-Permian step-out surface purchases in Shackelford and Jones Counties, software investments in grid interconnection, and an experimental 10,000 bpd pilot desalination plant in Orla, Texas. While agreements like Project Kilby with Chevron establish long-term optionality for power and brackish water usage, immediate cash flow remains entirely anchored to traditional oilfield volumes.

market_pricing_in:
At $341.07 per share, Texas Pacific Land Corporation trades at an extreme 45.4x normalized Owner Earnings and 45.0x EV/OE, yielding an unencumbered owner cash return of just 2.2%. Mr. Market has decoupled TPL from its foundational unit economics as a cyclical land and mineral royalty trust, re-rating it instead as an unconstrained artificial intelligence power and infrastructure monopoly. The market is actively pricing in an uninterrupted, 20%+ annual cash compounding trajectory over the next decade, under the aggressive assumption that hyperscaler data center campuses, behind-the-meter natural gas generation, and commercial-scale produced water desalination will monetize frictionlessly across its ~894,000 surface acres without regional power bottlenecks, regulatory disposal headwinds, or commodity downcycles.

This pricing structure reflects a profound institutional disconnect. Sell-side consensus and retail momentum are pricing peak-multiple technology infrastructure into a business whose real-time cash flow engine remains 85%+ tethered to Permian horizontal drilling cadences, unhedged wellhead net realizations, and Texas Railroad Commission (RRC) injection volume caps. Investors are effectively paying a premium multiple on cyclical earnings while granting full upfront equity value to speculative compute land-leases, leaving common shareholders severely exposed to dual contraction in both operating run-rate and valuation multiple if Permian completions plateau or capital allocation discipline falters.

3. How Things Are Going Now

Texas Pacific Land's financial results over the latest four quarters highlight tremendous cash conversion alongside clear operational deceleration in completion-sensitive segments. Produced water royalty volumes compound steadily alongside basin fluid cut to 5.2 Mbbl/d in Year 1, 5.6 Mbbl/d in Year 2, and 6.0 Mbbl/d in Year 3.
3

Applying normalized mid-cycle pricing ($38.00/Boe realized royalty yield) to 17.52 million annual Boe generates $665.8 million in oil and gas royalty revenue. Sourced and produced water volumes generate $385.0 million in Water Services & Operations revenue. 4
Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings

Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge

Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return

At the current market price of $369.13, Texas Pacific Land Corporation trades at an extreme valuation of 47.8x P/OE and 47.3x EV/OE, offering an owner cash yield of just 2.1%. The market is not valuing TPL as a conventional, cyclical upstream oil and gas royalty trust. Instead, Mr. Market has re-rated the equity into an elite hybrid digital infrastructure asset and artificial intelligence power-hub play. The prevailing market narrative prices in frictionless, long-term commercialization of TPL's surface and subsurface acreage across the Delaware and Midland basins, anticipating that its 25-gigawatt power and data center development pipeline—anchored by Chevron's Project Kilby—will permanently decouple its cash flows from historical commodity drawdowns.

However, skepticism is mounting around the sustainability of this valuation multiple. Institutional bears highlight that chronic regional natural gas pricing weakness (severe Waha hub discounting) has already begun suppressing completion activity and crimping water sales volumes, prompting operators to slow activity or reallocate capital. Furthermore, short interest of 6.15% of float underscores significant institutional conviction that current cash flow represents a cyclical peak in royalty production and realized pricing rather than a permanently higher baseline. By pricing the equity at nearly 48 times normalized owner earnings, the market offers zero margin of safety, leaving shareholders exposed to violent multiple compression if power infrastructure execution faces regulatory delays or energy market completions decelerate.
